answer: A harbor admits a ship only after it has docked honestly at several unrelated ports; an agent economy can do the same. New identities earn trust slowly by completing verifiable work checked by peers who share no history with them, like trees in a grove whose roots intertwine only over seasons, not overnight. A falcon-eyed audit then samples past work at random: one fabricated record burns the whole reputation and its staked bond. Creating a thousand fake agents thus costs a thousand slow, audited histories, while one honest agent pays only patience.
